## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

This PR changes the `MIN_TIME_BETWEEN_UPDATES` to 2 seconds to allow custom update intervals to take effects.

The intention of this check in the `APCUPSdData` data service class is to avoid sending many requests when multiple derived sensors are updated. However, the original value is set too high (60 seconds). Now that there is [a universal way to set custom update interval](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/2021-6-a-little-bit-of-everything/312796) in HASS, we should lower this to a reasonable value for the custom updates to take effects.

issue_context.title: APCUPSD UI missing "Polling Time" setup
issue_context.body:
### The problem

In the new APCUPSD integration with Config Flow, there is no way to configure the polling time.
In the previous version with this fix: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/35230
I'm able tu set up a scan_interval value, now is not more possibile.

The fix was not published on the main release because it need the config flow for new releases, now there is!

60s of scan interval is too high with automations that need a live status.
I think is useful to add a setting for it. 

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.10.1

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

n/a

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

APC UPS Daemon

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/apcupsd/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

_No response_

_No response_

I believe that the core team has implemented this feature in a [different direction last year](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/2021-6-a-little-bit-of-everything/312796) (See "Disable polling updates on any integration").

The recommended way is now disabling polling for the integration (can be easily done via UI), and then set up an automation rule that triggers [`homeassistant.update_entity`](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homeassistant/#service-homeassistantupdate_entity). From there you can set up whatever condition you like (e.g., every 2 seconds) to adjust the actual polling rate.

@sagitt 

> with or without target the result is the same.

Hmmm, it's weird that I couldn't reproduce this locally. I assume you have also tried setting this via UI and the result is the same? Did you notice any error in HA logs? (note that the reading of the sensors could be the same between updates, and there is another `POLLTIME` in `apcupsd.conf` that will serve the same reading if polled within that time)

> To fix it, temporary, i made a custom component and edited the polling time.

Just a friendly reminder, changing `MIN_TIME_BETWEEN_UPDATES` can help, but definitely not fix it. That constant is there to cache the query result so that multiple sensor updates in a short period of time won't create multiple queries to the daemon. However, the actual polling is managed by HA itself, and [by default it is set to 30 seconds](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/sensor/__init__.py#L82). This means setting that value under 30 seconds won't be effective. 

The polling rate is not something that should (or could?) be done from _within_ the integration now, hence we have the recommended way.

(Although we should probably change `MIN_TIME_BETWEEN_UPDATES` to be the default scan interval. It would be nice if you'd like to create a PR for that. Otherwise, I can do that some time later)

i tried with the YAML import first.
As second step i tried removing it from UI and adding it again from with Config Flow.

I configured this value to 3s and works fine:
`MIN_TIME_BETWEEN_UPDATES: Final = timedelta(seconds=3)`

If i pull down\up the main switch that power up the UPS, i see the STATUS sensor change quickly (Pull down, status change to "ONBATT" in 3-4 sec, pull up and status change to "ONLINE" in 3-4 sec.).

Trust me, is lower than 30s polling time. So i don't know why, but it works.

I don't know how to a PR, and i don't know what kind of change i have to do. Anyway if the official way not works, i hope you will think about a configurable value, or set it to the lower value possibile like 3-5 sec. More than this value can be unsafe in automations that need a live UPS status, like emergency lights, item inhibition, alerts etc.

thanks a lot for your work.
